## Model structure classification

Human raters classified models according to methodological structures.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-classification
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Classification of models by number of raters in total and agreement on model structure.

model_classifier <- classify_models(return_majority = FALSE) |> 
  distinct(model, classification, raters, votes, agreement) |> 
  group_by(model) |>
  mutate(final = classification[which.max(votes)]) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = classification, values_from = votes, values_fill = 0) |> 
  filter(model %in% unique(scores$Model)) |>
  select(Model = model, `Final classification` = final,
         Agreement = agreement, `Total raters` = raters, everything()) |>
  arrange(Agreement, Model)

model_classifier |> 
    kable()
```

## Variant phase identification

Genomic surveillance data were obtained from three sources: ECDC (covering 30 European countries), UKHSA (Great Britain), and the Swiss Federal Office of Public Health (Switzerland).
Variant lineages were mapped to six named phases in expected chronological order: Alpha, Delta, Omicron-BA.1, Omicron-BA.2, Omicron-BA.4/5, and Omicron-BQ/XBB.
For each country, we identified the first week in which each named variant exceeded 50% of sequenced samples.
We enforced chronological ordering by removing any out-of-sequence phases, then expanded phase assignments to all weeks by filling forward and backward from observed transition dates.
This per-location approach accounts for the fact that variant dominance dates differed substantially across European countries.
Where genomic surveillance data were too sparse to identify a transition (Hungary), we supplemented with epidemiological reports to set the Alpha-to-Delta transition date.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-variant-phases
#| fig-cap: "Variant phases identified by dominant variant in each location and week"

# see: R/utils-variants.R
variant_phases <- classify_variant_phases()
variant_phases |>
    ggplot(aes(x = target_end_date, y = location, fill = VariantPhase)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_brewer(type = "qual", palette = 2) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Location", fill = "Variant phase") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Epidemic growth window

<!-- S (#201) why growth is averaged over two weeks: windows of 1-4 weeks compared by how well past growth predicted realised growth over each forecast horizon, using observed data only, not the scores; 4 weeks (matching the longest horizon) worst for both outcomes; 1 week best for cases, 2 weeks for deaths; 2 weeks best single window across both, better than 3 (the four weeks the old +/-5% trend read) for both -->

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-growth-window
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Correlation between past epidemic growth and the growth that followed, by
#|   the number of weeks past growth was averaged over. Past growth: average
#|   weekly change in log(count + 1) over k weeks to the covariate week (ending
#|   eight days before the forecast date). Realised growth: average weekly
#|   change from the week ending the day before the forecast date to the target
#|   week at each horizon. Spearman correlation over each outcome, location and
#|   covariate week used by at least one forecast, with 90% intervals from
#|   resampling locations (200 draws). Grey band: three weeks, the window
#|   before this comparison.
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 7

# Spearman correlation by window k (x), small multiples by horizon, outcome by
# colour and direct label; observed data only, no scores
growth_obs <- c(Cases = "case", Deaths = "death") |>
  map(\(x) read_csv(here("data", paste0("observed-", x, ".csv")),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "epi_target") |>
  transmute(epi_target, location, date = target_end_date,
            ly = log(observed + 1))
# log(count + 1) w weeks after each week, joined on date
growth_shift <- function(w) {
  transmute(growth_obs, epi_target, location, date = date - weeks(w),
            !!paste0("ly_", w + 4) := ly)
}
covariate_weeks <- scores |>
  filter(!is.na(Horizon)) |>
  distinct(epi_target, location = as.character(Location),
           date = target_end_date - weeks(Horizon + 1))
growth_windows <- reduce(map(c(-4:-1, 1:5), growth_shift), left_join,
                         by = c("epi_target", "location", "date"),
                         .init = growth_obs) |>
  semi_join(covariate_weeks, by = c("epi_target", "location", "date"))
# ly is the covariate week t, ly_j the week t + (j - 4); ly_5 is the week
# ending the day before the forecast date
for (k in 1:4) {
  growth_windows[[paste0("past_", k)]] <-
    (growth_windows$ly - growth_windows[[paste0("ly_", 4 - k)]]) / k
  growth_windows[[paste0("future_", k)]] <-
    (growth_windows[[paste0("ly_", 5 + k)]] - growth_windows$ly_5) / k
}
growth_window_rho <- function(dat) {
  expand_grid(k = 1:4, h = 1:4) |>
    pmap(\(k, h) {
      dat |>
        group_by(epi_target) |>
        summarise(k = k, h = h,
                  rho = cor(.data[[paste0("past_", k)]],
                            .data[[paste0("future_", h)]],
                            method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
                  .groups = "drop")
    }) |>
    list_rbind()
}
set.seed(201)
growth_by_loc <- split(growth_windows, growth_windows$location)
growth_window_fit <- map(1:200, \(b) {
  growth_window_rho(bind_rows(sample(growth_by_loc, replace = TRUE)))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  group_by(epi_target, k, h) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(rho, 0.05), hi = quantile(rho, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(growth_window_rho(growth_windows),
            by = c("epi_target", "k", "h"))

dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.3)
growth_window_fit |>
  ggplot(aes(k, rho, colour = epi_target)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, colour = "#d4d4d4", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#7f7f7f", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), position = dodge) +
  geom_line(position = dodge, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(position = dodge, size = 1.6) +
  geom_text(data = filter(growth_window_fit, h == 4, k == 4),
            aes(label = epi_target), hjust = -0.25, size = 3,
            position = dodge) +
  facet_wrap(~ h, nrow = 1,
             labeller = labeller(h = \(x) paste("Horizon", x))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Cases = "#1a1a1a", Deaths = "#c0392b"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4, expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 1.3))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = "Weeks averaged over for past growth",
       y = "Spearman correlation with\nrealised growth") +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```
